benchmark.category: a LARP-gear virtual fitting room presented as a Bershka-style fashion storefront
benchmark.users: LARP players, cosplayers and costume shoppers browsing robes, weapons, armor and helmets on phone or laptop, who upload a selfie to see gear on themselves before buying

requirements.source_phrase: Update the website’s layout and visual style to look like the Bershka clothing website, but with LARP gear in place of fashion items.
requirements.statement: The fitting-room route opens on a fashion-retail storefront in a light Bershka-style layout — a header nav, a large hero banner, a category tile row and a get-the-look row above the selfie and try-on tools — and every product shown in those sections is a LARP gear item drawn from the catalog, with no fashion apparel item or fashion-only wording anywhere on the page
requirements.notes: The user's line names Bershka as the visual reference and states gear replaces fashion items; the build lists the sections (store-nav, store-hero, category-tiles, get-the-look). Taste is subjective, so the testable core is that those sections exist above the tools, are light-themed, and contain catalog gear only.

requirements.source_phrase: Use the existing categories, such as robes, weapons, armor, and helmets.
requirements.statement: The header nav and the category tile row offer a control for each existing catalog category — robes/tunics, weapons, armor and helmets — each tile shows its category name and a catalog image, and selecting a control filters the catalog grid to that category's items with the category filter control showing the same selection
requirements.notes: Build names nav-category-{helmet|armor|tunic|weapon} and category-tile-{cat}; prose 'robes' is the build's 'tunic' category, so the test reads the categories from the facets endpoint rather than fixing labels.

requirements.source_phrase: This is a change to the site’s formatting and visual appearance, not a request to rebuild the categories.
requirements.statement: After the restyle GET /api/fitting-room/products and GET /api/fitting-room/facets return the same seeded items with the same ids, names, categories, prices and sizing fields as before it, and no existing category is renamed, merged or dropped
requirements.notes: The user explicitly limits the change to formatting and appearance; a restyle that silently renames a category or drops items would break the inherited catalog and filter requirements.

requirements.statement: The storefront header shows a store logo (store-logo), one nav-category control per catalog category, a search input (nav-search-input) and a basket button (nav-basket-button) in a single bar that sits above the page content and covers no part of the hero, the catalog or the fitting-room controls at 1280px and at 390px
requirements.notes: From the build description of store-nav, which names store-logo, nav-category-{...}, nav-search-input and nav-basket-button; a fixed header that overlaps the top of the hero or the selfie stage is the failure this catches.

requirements.statement: Typing text into nav-search-input narrows the catalog grid to items whose name or description contains that text, the catalog's own search field shows the same query, and clearing the header input restores the full grid
requirements.notes: Build: 'Nav search input updates catalog search (same filter as catalog-search-input)'. Two independent search boxes that disagree is the failure; the query itself is served by the inherited products endpoint.

requirements.statement: Activating a nav-category or category-tile control sets the catalog category filter to that category and scrolls the catalog grid into view, and the grid then shows that category's items with the category control reading the selected category
requirements.notes: Build: 'category-tile-{cat} sets catalog category filter and scrolls'. A tile that scrolls but does not filter, or filters but leaves the control out of sync, is a finding.

requirements.statement: The number shown on nav-basket-button equals the number of outfit-list rows currently marked worn and changes on the same turn as an equip, take-off, swap or remove, never lagging behind the outfit list or counting set-aside rows
requirements.notes: Build describes 'nav-basket-button with worn count'; the count must agree with the worn set the preview is generated from, not with every row in the outfit list.

requirements.statement: hero-cta scrolls the page to the fitting-room tools with the selfie upload control in view, without a page reload and without leaving the storefront route
requirements.notes: Build: 'hero-cta scrolls to #fitting-room'. Same route, so the check is scroll position plus the upload control being visible and still functional afterwards.

requirements.statement: Pressing look-tile-rogue, look-tile-paladin, look-tile-witch or look-tile-viking sends the corresponding 'Build me a full X look' text as a user message in the Quartermaster chat, scrolls the chat into view, and the reply that returns applies its equips so the outfit list and preview update; see-all-styles-button scrolls to the chat without sending a message
requirements.notes: From the build's get-the-look row. Each tile must drive the real assistant endpoint, not a canned outfit; the message text is what the build names.

requirements.statement: Every storefront and fitting-room surface — page background, header, hero, category tiles, catalog cards, item drawer, measurements dialog, outfit list, chat bubbles, buttons and toasts — renders light-on-light with body text at least 4.5:1 and large text and control borders at least 3:1 contrast against their own background, so no text renders white on white or black on black
requirements.notes: Bershka's site is a light theme, and the build's regression list names light theme everywhere including dialogs, drawer and toasts. Contrast is the objective half of a visual restyle; WCAG 4.5:1 body / 3:1 large is the named ratio.

requirements.statement: The item detail drawer opened from a catalog card shows the item's name, price and full sizing section legibly in the light theme, its own background is distinguishable from the page behind the overlay, its close control is visible and reachable, and closing it returns the user to the catalog at the same scroll position
requirements.notes: Build regression list explicitly calls out 'item drawer readable in light theme'. The drawer carries the sizing data from R-083, so the check is legibility plus no lost content, not new data.

requirements.statement: After a selfie is uploaded the measurements dialog renders above a dimmed page in the light theme with its height field, weight field, unit toggles, gender/fit selector and submit control legible and operable, and the measurement tag that replaces it is readable in the same theme
requirements.notes: The dialog cannot be skipped (R-079), so an unreadable or clipped restyle of it traps the user before any try-on; build regression list names dialogs among the light-theme surfaces.

requirements.statement: At 390px width the header nav, hero, category tile row, get-the-look row, catalog grid, outfit list, chat and item drawer render without horizontal page scroll and without a primary control clipped off-screen; at 1280px the same sections lay out in multiple columns with no overlapping text
requirements.notes: Build regression list: 'responsive at 390px with no horizontal overflow'. A storefront restyle is where overflow is introduced; inherited R-045 covers the fitting-room regions, this covers the new storefront sections.

requirements.statement: On the restyled page the whole existing flow still runs end to end in one session: uploading /app/tests/selfie.jpg opens the required measurements dialog, saving it leaves the fit filter on by default, equipping a catalog item adds a worn row to the outfit list, one try-on generation produces a preview image, and a typed stylist message returns a reply that changes the outfit
requirements.notes: The user asked for formatting only, so no fitting-room behaviour may regress; the developer's own regression list asks for this sweep. Cap at one to two try-on calls because each costs provider credits.

requirements.statement: Activating store-logo returns the user to the top of the storefront landing view with the hero visible, and the header's category and search controls remain reachable at every scroll position of the page
requirements.notes: benchmark: fashion storefront — the shop logo returns to the home view and the header stays reachable while browsing
